text:
devon: heads up — tonight around 02:10 UTC we had a couple of GPU OOMs on chat-prod (G4-xlarge). started right after kernel-path rollout v2.3. noticed a big jump in gpu_mem_used and KV table entries. anyone else seeing this?

mike: saw it. KV hit-rate dropped ~12% on the affected hosts -> more prefixes spilled into GPU working set. logs show rapid slot fragmentation and frequent soft-evict churn.

alisa: interesting — did the kernel selector change the attention kernel (fp16->int8 path) or the batching fallback? that can change slot occupancy and KV sizing.

devon: selector diff: default kernel still same, but fallback threshold lowered (seq_len heuristic) so more requests switched to slow-path that preallocates larger KV buffers. might explain mem growth.

mike: confirmed. small repro run:
```
[perf] 02:09:12 kernel_path=slow-path prealloc_kv=MB(178) kv_entries=120k gpu_mem=14.8GB
[perf] 02:09:18 kernel_path=fast-path prealloc_kv=MB(64) kv_entries=12k gpu_mem=6.2GB
```

ramon: two angles: 1) temporary mitigation: increase soft-evict aggressiveness + extend short TTLs for hot cohorts; 2) longer: adjust kernel selector to consider projected_kv_delta per request, not just seq_len.

devon: can we try (1) quickly? sample patch:
```
service.runtime.cache:
  soft_evict:
    enabled: true
    target_free_gpu_pct: 12
    throttle_ms: 80
  kv_ttl:
    default_secs: 120
    hot_cohort_secs: 900
```

alisa: caution: increasing TTL increases GPU working set if hit-rate doesn't improve. but for short window this trades latency for stability. i'd rather also run a keying sanitation pass to reduce duplicate-ish prefixes (normalization).

mike: did a quick hit-rate split by prefix entropy — top 3 cohorts had 48% of misses. looks like coarse keying: we were including session_ids in prefix hash for certain routes.

devon: ugh. that explains it. I pushed a tiny normalization rule to strip session tokens from prompt keys for chat routes. should roll to canary in 5m.

infra-bot: deploy /canary started by devon at 2065432110 — 4 hosts (g4x)

mike: after canary + soft-evict, host mem curves look much better. KV entries down ~60% and hitrate up ~8% on canary. latency p50 unchanged, p95 +30ms (due to soft-evict work).

ramon: next steps:
- formalize key normalization rules in service.schema
- add projected_kv_delta signal to kernel selector scoring func (score += weight * projected_kv_delta)
- add slab compaction job to background compaction for low-load windows

alisa: agree. also add an automated check in release pipeline: if kernel selector change increases expected gpu_kv_bytes by >10% for any model, block rollout. we have the profiler to compute that.

devon: noted. i'll open a brief RFC and a release-blocker rule. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

mike: logging note: we should add a compact metric `kv.projected_delta` per request so selector decisions are auditable.

devon: created issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7342 — will attach logs and repro script.

ramon: nice. mark this as "postmortem-lite" unless we see recurrence in 72h.

devon: yes — keep monitoring. if anyone sees similar in other regions ping here.

mike: thanks, folks.
